judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'African American Civil War Memorial' result card (a link). I re-ran a Tab walk on the live page (2026-10-23, Edge headless, 1280x800). When focused, this result card moves up a few pixels and gets a 4 px #2491ff outline with outline-offset 0. The outline sits just outside the card, on the white page that the card's box-shadow (0 3px 15px rgba(0,0,0,.2)) tints. The pixels right next to the outline on the outside are #eaeaea to #f6f6f6, which gives 2.66 to 2.96:1. Inside, it borders the photo (light sky or water at about 1.6 to 2.1:1) and, only along the bottom, the black text panel. The Understanding document says an outline drawn outside a component has to contrast with the background it sits on, and here that background is below 3:1 everywhere next to the indicator. Against plain #fff it would be 3.2:1, so the margin is small, but the colours actually rendered fail 1.4.11.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Back to top' Bootstrap btn-link in the pagination row. On the live page its focus style is outline:none plus a 4 px box-shadow ring of rgba(49,132,253,.5). On white, that ring renders as #98c1fe. Focus changes nothing else: no underline and no colour change; only the ~1260 ring pixels differ. #98c1fe against the white background around it and inside it is about 1.7 to 1.8:1. The author styled this indicator, so it needs 3:1 and fails 1.4.11. It is visible, so 2.4.7 passes.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'View all' btn-link next to 'Back to top' and has the same focus style. Outline is none and the only focus cue is a 4 px rgba(49,132,253,.5) box-shadow ring, which renders as #98c1fe on white (about 1.8:1). I confirmed on the live page that the ring is the only pixel change. An author-styled indicator under 3:1 fails 1.4.11.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Touchpoints' link in the grey (#f0f0f0) footer strip of the 'Was this page helpful?' form. Its text is already underlined, so focus adds only a 4 px #2491ff outline with offset 0, and only those ~728 pixels change. The outline sits mostly on the #f0f0f0 strip on both sides, at 2.81:1. Only its top edge pokes into the white form area, at 3.2:1. Against the background it is drawn on, the indicator is below 3:1, so it fails 1.4.11.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Search or ask anything' label in the DOI search/chat launcher pill at the top right. On the live page at 1280x1024, I applied the WCAG text-spacing values (line-height 1.5, letter 0.12em, word 0.16em, paragraph 2em). The nowrap label grew from 161 to 215 px. The button stays a fixed 220 px, and its div.abd-popover wrapper has overflow:hidden, so the visible text is cut to 'Search or ask anythi'. Clipped text under the spacing override is the documented failure F104, so this fails 1.4.12 as reported.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the checked 'List' radio of the List/Map view switch. The radio is visually hidden (1x1 px) and its label 'List' is the visible control. On the live page Tab lands on it with :focus-visible true. The label has no focus style (outline none, no shadow), and the hidden input's outline cannot be seen. The focused and blurred screenshots differ by 0 pixels in the whole viewport. There is no visible focus indicator, which fails 2.4.7.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Entrance Passes / America the Beautiful Pass Series' promo tile link. I re-ran a keyboard walk on the live page at 1280x800 with no mouse hover. The link gets focus and matches :focus-visible, and its computed style has a 4 px #2491ff outline. The parent div.ContentPromo is exactly the link's size and has overflow:hidden, so the outline is clipped. Comparing screenshots of the focused and blurred states showed 0 changed pixels in the whole viewport. The image zoom you see on these tiles happens on mouse hover only. A keyboard user gets no visible focus indicator, which fails 2.4.7, as the finding says.
